body:
That bug (or feature even?) appears to happen on non-empty projects as well.

I usually start projects on MacOS using terminal from within the project directory by simply calling `open project.godot` (`open` is Mac specific and automatically resolves to the application being mapped to the file type) but for some reason it started an older Godot version that I have installed. Thus to open the project I used `godot -e` instead which starts the current version 4.6.

I then got the exact same error:

```bash
$ godot -e
Godot Engine v4.6.stable.official.89cea1439 - https://godotengine.org
OpenGL API 4.1 Metal - 90.5 - Compatibility - Using Device: Apple - Apple M1 Max

ERROR: Condition "p_name.is_empty()" is true.
   at: set_name (scene/main/node.cpp:1432)
```

It doesn't really bother me since it's not affecting anything, apparently. Just wanted to confirm that this error exists (which I am sure nobody doubted in the first place, but yeah… 😅).

All my other projects are not yet migrated to the latest 4.6 release so I can't test them right now.

My specs:
Apple M1 Max, 32 GB, macOS Tahoe (26.2)
